targets.note: a first comparison with the bench asks whether both sides agree on the width within a decade. Extracting a stiffness to the per cent is a later, confirm revision, and the record length it needs is what this one's A2 returns as a relation

estimation.note: the registered estimator: the per-axis standard deviation of x and y about the record's own mean over the declared record_length after startup_discard. The bias correction, the histogram and the kurtosis ride on the same trace and are not the estimator

new_facts.claim: On this workstation trap_hoomd_backend costs about 6 microseconds of wall clock per integration step for one overdamped sphere in a harmonic trap with the fluid at rest.
new_facts.validity_conditions: trap_hoomd_backend as committed at the time of run-20260923-102-s2, one particle, a save every twenty steps, one run of 52500 steps on 2026-09-24 while other sessions shared the machine. Not a per-particle cost for N above one.

numbers.name: temperature
numbers.note: the room's reading; not established to be the sample's

numbers.name: bead_diameter
numbers.note: the tracer in the bottle in use, measured by the operator

numbers.name: trap_stiffness_operating
numbers.note: the one stiffness this revision runs, the double well's soft trap

numbers.name: integration_timestep_op
numbers.note: A1's noise bound binds, with S4's margin for the rounding of tau

numbers.name: save_interval_op
numbers.note: 20 steps a frame: the largest whole number of steps under A4's ceiling of a tenth of gamma/k_t that is a clean one-figure value, so every frame falls on a step

numbers.name: startup_discard_op
numbers.note: 125 frames: the first whole number of frames at or above ten relaxation times. The particle starts at the trap centre and its distribution relaxes over gamma/k_t, so ten of them leave a residual far below a per mille. Declared in advance, never chosen after seeing the data

numbers.name: record_length_op
numbers.note: the averaging window after the start-up: twice A2's floor. The observable's registered window, and the bench's record length too

numbers.name: width_acceptance_op
numbers.note: the success band, three of the record's own standard errors, fixed before the run

numbers.name: thermal_width_predicted
numbers.note: sqrt(k_B*T/k_t) from the plan's inputs: the per-axis width the model predicts, and the number the bench width is compared against. One figure because the inputs are declared that way; the comparison that carries precision is the ratio in criteria_evaluation, set by the run

numbers.name: thermal_width_scatter_predicted
numbers.note: the width's standard error from one record of the declared length, sigma*sqrt(tau/(2T))

numbers.name: max_step_displacement
numbers.note: the largest single-step displacement, which the divergence criterion watches against the bead diameter

numbers.name: width_deviation_in_decades
numbers.note: |log10(measured width / predicted width)|, the larger of x and y: how many decades apart

numbers.name: relative_deviation_of_width_from_equipartition
numbers.note: the larger of |x| and |y| width over sqrt(k_B*T/k_t), corrected for the record's expected low bias, minus one. x read 0.9849 and y 0.9980 of the prediction, -0.31 and -0.04 of the record's own scatter. NOT EVIDENCE ABOUT ANY TRAP: k_t went in

numbers.name: integration_timestep_actual
numbers.note: simulated time over the integer step count

numbers.name: save_interval_actual
numbers.note: simulated time over the number of intervals between saved frames

numbers.name: record_length_actual
numbers.note: the span of frames the estimator read, after startup_discard

numbers.name: cost_per_step_measured
numbers.note: 0.339 s over 52500 steps of the integration loop alone, on trap_hoomd_backend, one bead, fluid at rest

assumptions.statement: The double well's soft trap, 0.5 pN/um, is the one stiffness this revision runs, because it is the first input the double well needs.
assumptions.falsifier: the bench reporting that its lowest usable dial setting is far stiffer moves it

kb_refs.claim: The particles in the bottle in use have a diameter of 5 micrometres, with a coefficient of variation no greater than 2 per cent, measured directly by the operator on 2026-09-19.
Dynamic viscosity of pure water near 293 K is of order one millipascal second, and it changes by roughly two percent per kelvin in that neighbourhood.

The laboratory's ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius, read off a thermometer by the operator. It is a reading and not a setpoint, and it is the room's rather than the sample's -- which is what makes it an operator reading at E3 and not a calibration at E2.
